site.tagline: A calmer space to understand the mind.
site.intro: Mindful Tattva is a student-led psychology club at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj University, creating room for curiosity, compassionate conversations and the small practices that help us feel more human.
site.announcement: A student-led space for reflection, connection & growth
site.aboutHeading: We make room for curiosity, care and community.
site.aboutBody: Our club brings psychology out of the textbook and into everyday life. Through conversations, workshops, hands-on activities and shared experiences, Mindful Tattva invites students to look inward, connect with others and grow with intention.
site.clubDescription: Mindful Tattva is a student-led psychology club under the Department of Applied Social Science at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj University. We create welcoming spaces for students to explore psychology, mental wellbeing, relationships, identity, resilience and the everyday science of being human.
site.mission: To make psychology approachable, relevant and rooted in compassion through student-led conversations, workshops, peer learning and community initiatives.
site.vision: A campus community where curiosity about the mind becomes empathy in action.
site.memberBenefits: Members can participate in workshops, discussion circles, awareness initiatives, hands-on activities, peer learning and future collaborations organised by Mindful Tattva.
site.joiningIntro: Join a thoughtful student community and help shape the next chapter of Mindful Tattva.
site.memberVision: We imagine Mindful Tattva as a living student space where every member can bring curiosity, care and creativity to the psychology of everyday life.

site.contactNote: Have an idea, want to collaborate, or simply want to be part of the next circle? We would love to hear from you.

awareness.title: Not everyone who looks fine, is fine.
awareness.stat: About 1 in 7 people aged 10–19 lives with a mental health condition.
awareness.body: Most struggles do not arrive as a crisis. They arrive as a student who stopped replying in the group chat, skipped two lectures, or laughs a little too hard to avoid a question. On a campus this size, that student is almost always sitting within three seats of us.
awareness.takeaway: Notice the quiet changes in the people around you, and ask once — properly.

awareness.title: Stress arrives in the body before it arrives in words.
awareness.stat: Half of all mental health conditions begin by the age of 14.
awareness.body: A racing heart, tight shoulders, a headache that returns every evening, food that either disappears or becomes a comfort, sleep that never really rests. When the nervous system stays switched on for months, attention, memory and patience pay the bill — and we usually blame ourselves instead.
awareness.takeaway: Long, slow breathing and an early conversation with a counsellor are not extra. They are the basics.

awareness.title: Being heard by one person changes the weight of a day.
awareness.stat: Students who feel connected on campus report better mental health than those who feel alone.
awareness.body: Not advice, not a lecture, not a comparison — just someone who stays in the room while you say the difficult sentence out loud. That is why the club exists: a bench, a chai, a five-minute honest conversation. Talking about mental health is not attention-seeking. It is maintenance.
awareness.takeaway: You do not need the right words. You only need to start.

awareness.title: Small habits, repeated gently, keep us steady.
awareness.stat: Sleep, movement, sunlight, water, one honest journal line and one real conversation a day.
awareness.body: None of these is a cure, and none of them replaces professional help — but together they make the hard weeks shorter. Pick one, keep it small enough that you cannot fail it, and let it be enough for today. Progress is rarely dramatic; it is usually boring, and it works.
awareness.takeaway: Ask for help early. Everybody needs it sometimes.
